intelligence.essence: Shawn's direction, in his words: spec it out — engineer the project system so it's highly effective; we must produce more and waste less (right now we're wasting a lot and producing very little — reverse that); and we must be aware of what we're producing and able to SEE it — that's what the project page is about. The spec (~/workspace/project-intelligence/SPEC.md v1) designs one loop — Produce → Prove → Publish → See — on top of what already exists: CPI state, the 15-minute refresh, the Smart Ledger, and the Projects page. Its core law: every act of work ends as a visible state change with proof, or it counts as waste — and the project page shows production and waste side by side, always current, maintained by the AIs as protocol, never typed in by the human.
intelligence.human_view: The math is counts, not adjectives. Production = a verified state transition to done-proven (the same event the Smart Ledger chains). Waste = activity that produced no transition and no evidence. The ratio — activity ÷ production — was audited at 173:1 on 2026-10-22; the target is under 60:1 by 2026-10-30, published daily. The spec names six wastes, each with a detector and a cure: zero-output loops, built-but-invisible work, aging items, duplicate work, report churn, and verification debt. The page gains a Production board next to the Intelligence board: today's landings and ratio in one human sentence, a 7-day trend strip, and a Waste panel that names aging items (with days standing still) and zero-output loops (with run counts) — or honestly says "none today." What waits on Shawn is pinned at the top, because his attention is the scarcest resource in the system and the page spends it first.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a workshop with a big board on the wall. Every time someone finishes making something real, they pin its picture on the board with a little tag showing where it is. If someone spent all day running around but finished nothing, the board shows that too — a list that says "ran all day, finished nothing." Nobody has to write reports; the board just always shows what got made and what got wasted. The rule of the workshop: if it's not on the board with its tag, it didn't happen.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like a good kitchen ledger. What came in, what went to the table, what spoiled in the pantry — all written down where everyone can see it. Nothing fancy: you cook, you serve, you write it in the book. If a bag of flour sat untouched for a week, the book shows it, and somebody deals with it. A house run this way stops wasting food without anyone giving speeches about wasting food — the book does the talking.
intelligence.naya_view: Engineering notes. The refresh computes a `production` block into state (transitions today/7d, done-proven total reconciling with the Intelligence strip, Smart Ledger tip, activity count from the census instrument, ratio — null until both sides honestly exist, never faked), plus aging (no transition ≥3 days) and zero-output loops (runs>0, transitions=0, 24h). The publisher projects items + production into the NayaPOWER project; the page renders Intelligence + Production boards and prints its own "intelligence as of" stamp — stale data that looks fresh is the one unforgivable defect in this system. The director runs the day from the page; any question the page can't answer is a spec defect filed as an intel item the same day. Acceptance is the Page Test: one full working day run exclusively from the project page (first run 2026-10-24), plus three-way reconciliation (page == state == Ledger tip) at every landing. The v2 build already in flight absorbed §4/§6 by director's instruction the same hour the spec was written.
intelligence.ai_view: This morning's assessment named the disease (173 actions per outcome) and tonight's Fourteen Questions named the interface. This spec is the treatment plan wired into the product itself: instead of productivity being a report somebody writes, it becomes a property of the page everybody already looks at. When waste is visible and named — with its owner and its age — it stops being a culture problem and becomes a work item. And when production is the same board, the team can finally see the ratio move as they change how they work, which is the only way a ratio ever really moves.

machine_view.title: Produce More, Waste Less — and See Both: the Project Intelligence Spec
machine_view.machine_section: SPEC: PROJECT-INTELLIGENCE v1. LOOP: PRODUCE→PROVE→PUBLISH→SEE. DEFINITIONS: production_unit := verified transition to done-proven == one Smart Ledger entry (keyed by item id, counted once). activity_unit := census instrument count. ratio := activity/production per UTC day. BASELINE: 173:1 (2026-10-22 audit). TARGET: <60:1 by 2026-10-30. WASTE CLASSES: W1 zero-output loop (runs≥20/24h, transitions=0) · W2 built-but-invisible (no live proof 24h) · W3 aging (no transition ≥3d) · W4 duplicate claim · W5 report churn (no transition, no decision) · W6 verification debt (>1 director pass). GUARDS: publisher failure-isolated; ratio null when unmeasured; transitions without evidence rejected structurally; TEST data never enters counts. ACCEPTANCE: PAGE_TEST 2026-10-24; three-way reconcile page==state==ledger.
